title: Gabber's degree-zero criterion for etale sheaves of sets
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Suppose that for every sheaf of sets $G$ on the underlying Zariski space of $X$, the canonical restriction $\Gamma(X,G)\to\Gamma(Z,i^{-1}_{\mathrm{Zar}}G)$ is bijective, with topological inverse image as in [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]. Suppose also that for every finite morphism $h:X'\to X$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], the same assertion holds for the base-changed closed immersion $i':Z'=Z\times_XX'\to X'$ and every Zariski sheaf of sets on $X'$. Then for every sheaf of sets $F$ on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] of $X$, the canonical restriction $\Gamma(X,F)\to\Gamma(Z,i^{-1}_{\mathrm{et}}F)$ is bijective, where $i^{-1}_{\mathrm{et}}$ is etale inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image].

source.place: Lemma Tag 09ZF (lemma-gabber-h0), lines 14974-15080, hypotheses (1), (2) and conclusion; proof uses finite surjective refinement from More on Morphisms and finite descent from Remark Tag 09Z3

proof.text: *Notation.* For a morphism of schemes $e:T\to S$ and a sheaf of sets $G$ on $S_{\Et}$ write $e^{-1}G$ for the etale inverse image and $e^*s\in(e^{-1}G)(U\times_ST)$ for the pullback of $s\in G(U)$ by the unit, and $c_{e,e'}$ for the composition isomorphisms, all as in [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units]; the restriction map of the statement is $s\mapsto i^*s$ on $\Gamma(X,F)$ ($X\times_XZ=Z$). For a finite morphism $h:X'\to X$ put $Z'=Z\times_XX'$, with the projections $i':Z'\to X'$ and $h_Z:Z'\to Z$, so $i\circ h_Z=h\circ i'$. Then $i'$ is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], $h_Z$ is finite [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] (a), and if $h$ is surjective so is $h_Z$ [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. The identity of $X$ is finite (affine, with identity ring maps) [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and for it $Z'=Z$, $i'=i$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09ZF, proof, third paragraph (notation i^{-1}s) and fourth paragraph (Z' = X' x_X Z, i' the base change of i)

proof.text: *Injectivity on $X$ and on every finite $X'$* (source, second paragraph). Let $h:X'\to X$ be finite and $G$ a sheaf of sets on $X'_{\Et}$. Then $\Gamma(X',G)\to\Gamma(Z',i'^{-1}G)$, $s\mapsto i'^*s$, is injective. Indeed, by [lem-weil-pbc-gabber-zariski-etale-restriction-injective] for the closed immersion $i'$ and $G$, this map is the composite of $\eta^{\rm Zar}_{X'}:\Gamma(X',G_{\rm Zar})\to\Gamma(Z',i'^{-1}_{\rm Zar}G_{\rm Zar})$ with the injective map $\beta_{Z'}$; and $\eta^{\rm Zar}_{X'}$ is bijective by hypothesis (2) of the statement applied to $h$ and the Zariski sheaf of sets $G_{\rm Zar}$ (by hypothesis (1) when $h=\mathrm{id}_X$). In particular (with $h=\mathrm{id}_X$, $G=F$) the map $\Gamma(X,F)\to\Gamma(Z,i^{-1}F)$ is injective.

*Every nonempty closed subset $T\subseteq X$ meets $i(Z)$* (source, fourth paragraph: 'by assumption (1) applied to the sheaf $(T	o X)_*\underline{\mathbf Z}$'; we use the two-element set). Let $T\subseteq X$ be closed and nonempty and suppose $T\cap i(Z)=\emptyset$. Let $\mathcal L$ be the sheaf of sets $W\mapsto\{$locally constant maps $W\cap T	o\{0,1\}\}$ on $X$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-constant-stalks] (0). The constant maps $0,1\in\mathcal L(X)$ are different since $T
eq\emptyset$. For $z\in Z$ the stalk $(i^{-1}_{m Zar}\mathcal L)_z$ is in bijection with $\mathcal L_{i(z)}$ [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-stalk], which has exactly one element because $i(z)
otin T$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-constant-stalks] (b). Hence $\eta^{m Zar}_X(0)$ and $\eta^{m Zar}_X(1)$ have the same germ at every point of $Z$ and are equal [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-sections-determined-by-germs], contradicting the bijectivity of $\Gamma(X,\mathcal L)	o\Gamma(Z,i^{-1}_{m Zar}\mathcal L)$ in hypothesis (1). So $T\cap i(Z)
eq\emptyset$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09ZF, proof, fourth paragraph: 'Observe that every nonempty closed subscheme T of X meets Z by assumption (1)'

proof.text: *Local form of a section of $i^{-1}F$* (source: 'By construction of $i^{-1}_{small}\mathcal F$'). Let $t\in\Gamma(Z,i^{-1}F)$. Write $i^{-1}F=(i_pF)^\#$ with $i_pF(V)=\varinjlim_{(U,\varphi)\in\mathcal I_V^{op}}F(U)$, $\mathcal I_V$ the pairs of $U$ etale over $X$ and a $Z$-morphism $\varphi:V\to U\times_XZ$, with coprojections $\iota_{(U,\varphi)}$ and sheafification map $\theta$ [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction] (2), for the functor $U\mapsto U\times_XZ$ of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] (1). By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] there are an etale covering $\{V_j\to Z\}_{j\in J}$ and $\sigma_j\in i_pF(V_j)$ with $t|_{V_j}=\theta(\sigma_j)$. The category $\mathcal I_{V_j}^{op}$ is filtered [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-pullback-sets-left-exact] (2), since $X_{\Et}$ has finite limits and $U\mapsto U\times_XZ$ commutes with them [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] (2), (3); so $\sigma_j=\iota_{(U_j,\varphi_j)}(s_j)$ for some $(U_j,\varphi_j)$ and $s_j\in F(U_j)$ [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] (1). By the definition of the restriction maps of $i_pF$, $\iota_{(U_j,\varphi_j)}(s_j)$ is the restriction along $\varphi_j:V_j\to U_j\times_XZ$ of $\iota_{(U_j,\mathrm{id})}(s_j)$, and $\theta(\iota_{(U_j,\mathrm{id})}(s_j))=i^*s_j$ is the unit; as $\theta$ is a morphism of presheaves, $t|_{V_j}=(i^*s_j)|_{V_j}$, the restriction along $\varphi_j$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09ZF, proof, fourth paragraph, first sentence

proof.text: *Shrinking $U_j$ so that $t|_{U_j\times_XZ}=i^*s_j$.* The morphism $\varphi_j:V_j\to U_j\times_XZ$ is a morphism of schemes etale over $Z$, hence etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (3), so its image $O_j$ is open [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map]. The projection $U_j\times_XZ\to U_j$ is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], a homeomorphism onto a closed subset carrying the subspace topology [def-weil-closed-immersion], so $O_j=U'_j\times_XZ$ for an open $U'_j\subseteq U_j$. Replace $U_j$ by $U'_j$ (etale over $X$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1), (2)), $s_j$ by $s_j|_{U'_j}$ and $\varphi_j$ by its corestriction; the equality of the previous step persists by [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] (0). Now $\varphi_j$ is surjective, so $\{\varphi_j:V_j\to U_j\times_XZ\}$ is a covering of $Z_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Since $V_j\to Z$ factors as $V_j\to U_j\times_XZ\to Z$, the sections $t|_{U_j\times_XZ}$ and $i^*s_j$ have the same restriction along $\varphi_j$, hence are equal by the sheaf condition for this one-member covering [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets].

source.place: Lemma Tag 09ZF, proof, fourth paragraph: 'Since V_j -> U_j x_X Z is etale, the image is an open subscheme ... we conclude that t|_{U_j x_X Z} = i^{-1}s_j'

proof.text: *$\coprod_jU_j\to X$ is surjective etale.* Let $U=\coprod_jU_j$ (disjoint union of schemes, each $U_j$ an open subscheme of $U$) with $u:U\to X$ given by the structure maps; $u$ is etale since each $U_j\to X$ is [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-on-source]. Its image $\bigcup_ju(U_j)$ is open [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map]. It contains $i(Z)$: for $z\in Z$ there are $j$ and $v\in V_j$ over $z$ (the $V_j$ cover $Z$), and the image of $v$ under $V_j\to U_j\times_XZ\to U_j$ lies over $i(z)$. Its complement is closed and disjoint from $i(Z)$, hence empty by step 2. So $u$ is surjective and etale, and $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09ZF, proof, fourth paragraph: 'Thus we see that coprod U_j -> X is surjective'

proof.text: *Finite refinement.* By [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-refinement-etale-cover] applied to $u$ there are a finite, finitely presented, surjective $h:X'\to X$, a finite open covering $X'=\bigcup_aW_a$ and $X$-morphisms $\phi_a:W_a\to U$ with $u\circ\phi_a=h|_{W_a}$. The opens $W_\alpha=\phi_a^{-1}(U_j)$, $\alpha=(a,j)$, cover $X'$; put $j(\alpha)=j$ and let $g_\alpha:W_\alpha\to U_{j(\alpha)}$ be the restriction of $\phi_a$, an $X$-morphism: $(U_{j(\alpha)}\to X)\circ g_\alpha=h|_{W_\alpha}$. (This is the refinement $X'=\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}W_\alpha$, $j:A\to J$ of the source.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 09ZF, proof, fourth paragraph: 'By More on Morphisms, Lemma 09Z0 we can find a finite surjective morphism X' -> X ... g_alpha : W_alpha -> U_{j(alpha)} over X'

proof.text: *The local sections $s'_\alpha$ and the section $t'$ on $Z'$.* Put $F'=h^{-1}F$ and $e=i\circ h_Z=h\circ i':Z'\to X$. For each $\alpha$, $\gamma_\alpha=(g_\alpha,\mathrm{incl}):W_\alpha\to U_{j(\alpha)}\times_XX'$ is a morphism of $X'_{\Et}$; let $s'_\alpha=(h^*s_{j(\alpha)})|_{W_\alpha}\in F'(W_\alpha)$, the restriction along $\gamma_\alpha$. Let $\kappa=c_{h,i',F}^{-1}\circ c_{i,h_Z,F}:h_Z^{-1}i^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}i'^{-1}F'$ [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] (1) and $t'=\kappa(h_Z^*t)\in\Gamma(Z',i'^{-1}F')$. Claim: $t'|_{W_\alpha\cap Z'}=i'^*s'_\alpha$. Write $j=j(\alpha)$. Applying $h_Z^*$ to $t|_{U_j\times_XZ}=i^*s_j$ (step 4) gives $(h_Z^*t)|_{U_j\times_XZ'}=h_Z^*(i^*s_j)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] (0); by (1), $c_{i,h_Z,F}(h_Z^*i^*s_j)=e^*s_j=c_{h,i',F}(i'^*h^*s_j)$, and $c$ commutes with restrictions, so $t'|_{U_j\times_XZ'}=i'^*(h^*s_j)$ in $(i'^{-1}F')((U_j\times_XX')\times_{X'}Z')$. Restricting along $\gamma_\alpha\times_{X'}Z':W_\alpha\times_{X'}Z'=W_\alpha\cap Z'\to(U_j\times_XX')\times_{X'}Z'$ and using (0) once more gives $t'|_{W_\alpha\cap Z'}=i'^*s'_\alpha$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09ZF, proof, fourth paragraph: 'Denote F' the pullback of F to X'_etale ... Then t'|_{W_alpha x_X Z} is equal to (i')^{-1}s'_alpha by construction'

proof.text: *$t'$ comes from a section $s'\in\Gamma(X',F')$.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-gabber-zariski-etale-restriction-injective] to $i':Z'\to X'$ and $F'$: $\beta':i'^{-1}_{\rm Zar}F'_{\rm Zar}\to(i'^{-1}F')_{\rm Zar}$ is injective on every open and $\beta'(\eta^{\rm Zar}_W(s))=i'^*s$. Put $\sigma_\alpha=\eta^{\rm Zar}_{W_\alpha}(s'_\alpha)$ on $W_\alpha\cap Z'$; then $\beta'(\sigma_\alpha)=i'^*s'_\alpha=t'|_{W_\alpha\cap Z'}$ by step 7. On $W_\alpha\cap W_{\alpha'}\cap Z'$ the restrictions of $\sigma_\alpha,\sigma_{\alpha'}$ have the same image $t'|$ under the injective $\beta'$, so they agree; as the $W_\alpha\cap Z'$ cover $Z'$ they glue to $\sigma\in\Gamma(Z',i'^{-1}_{\rm Zar}F'_{\rm Zar})$, a sheaf [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (3), and $\beta'(\sigma)=t'$ because both sides restrict to $t'|_{W_\alpha\cap Z'}$ on each $W_\alpha\cap Z'$ (sheaf condition of $(i'^{-1}F')_{\rm Zar}$). Hypothesis (2) for the finite $h$ and the Zariski sheaf $F'_{\rm Zar}$ gives $s'\in F'_{\rm Zar}(X')=\Gamma(X',F')$ with $\eta^{\rm Zar}_{X'}(s')=\sigma$, hence $i'^*s'=\beta'(\sigma)=t'$. (So $t'$ is a section of the subsheaf $i'^{-1}(F'|_{X'_{Zar}})$, as the source says.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 09ZF, proof, fourth paragraph: 'We conclude that t' is a section of the subsheaf ... By assumption (2) the section t' comes from a section s''

proof.text: *The two pullbacks of $s'$ to $X''=X'\times_XX'$ agree.* Let $p_1,p_2:X''\to X'$ be the projections and $h_1=h\circ p_1=h\circ p_2$, finite as a composite of a base change of $h$ and $h$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] (a), [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition]. Put $Z''=Z\times_XX''$ with $i'':Z''\to X''$, let $q_k:Z''\to Z'$ be the base change of $p_k$ ($i'\circ q_k=p_k\circ i''$) and $r=h_Z\circ q_1=h_Z\circ q_2:Z''\to Z$ (both are the projection to $Z$). Let $x_k=c_{h,p_k,F}(p_k^*s')\in\Gamma(X'',h_1^{-1}F)$; we show $x_1=x_2$. By step 1 for $h_1$ and $h_1^{-1}F$ it suffices that $i''^*x_1=i''^*x_2$, and, $c_{h_1,i'',F}$ being bijective, that $y_k:=c_{h_1,i'',F}(i''^*x_k)$ do not depend on $k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] (0), (2) for $(h,p_k,i'')$ and (1) for $F'$: $y_k=c_{h_1,i''}\bigl(i''^{-1}(c_{h,p_k})(i''^*p_k^*s')\bigr)=c_{h,p_ki''}\bigl(c_{p_k,i''}(i''^*p_k^*s')\bigr)=c_{h,p_ki''}\bigl((p_ki'')^*s'\bigr)$. As $p_ki''=i'q_k$, (1) for $F'$, (2) for $(h,i',q_k)$ and (0) give $y_k=c_{h,i'q_k}\bigl(c_{i',q_k}(q_k^*i'^*s')\bigr)=c_{e,q_k}\bigl(q_k^*c_{h,i'}(i'^*s')\bigr)$. By step 8 and the definition of $t'$, $c_{h,i'}(i'^*s')=c_{h,i'}(t')=c_{i,h_Z}(h_Z^*t)$, and then (0), (2) for $(i,h_Z,q_k)$ and (1) for $i^{-1}F$ give $y_k=c_{e,q_k}\bigl(q_k^*c_{i,h_Z}(h_Z^*t)\bigr)=c_{i,h_Zq_k}\bigl(c_{h_Z,q_k}(q_k^*h_Z^*t)\bigr)=c_{i,r}(r^*t)$, independent of $k$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09ZF, proof, fourth paragraph: 'By the injectivity proved in the second paragraph, we conclude that the two pullbacks of s' to X' x_X X' are the same (after all this is true for the pullbacks of t' to Z' x_Z Z')'

proof.text: *Descent and conclusion.* By step 9 and [lem-weil-pbc-sets-finite-surjective-descent] for the finite surjective $h$ and $F$ there is $s\in\Gamma(X,F)$ with $h^*s=s'$. Then $i^*s=t$ (this check is left implicit in the source): by [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] (1), $c_{i,h_Z}(h_Z^*i^*s)=e^*s=c_{h,i'}(i'^*h^*s)=c_{h,i'}(i'^*s')=c_{h,i'}(t')=c_{i,h_Z}(h_Z^*t)$ (step 8 and the definition of $t'$), so $h_Z^*(i^*s)=h_Z^*t$; as $h_Z:Z'\to Z$ is finite and surjective (step 0), the injectivity in [lem-weil-pbc-sets-finite-surjective-descent] for $h_Z$ and the sheaf $i^{-1}F$ gives $i^*s=t$. Hence $\Gamma(X,F)\to\Gamma(Z,i^{-1}F)$ is surjective; it is injective by step 1, so it is bijective.
